title: Investigate tokens/sec degradation with first-byte jitter across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Multiple customers reported a sudden drop in tokens/sec and increased TTFT beginning 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. The behavior spans Hosted, Dedicated, and several Private deployments (EU and us-west clusters). Symptoms include elevated time-to-first-token for small requests, and a persistent 30-50% reduction in sustained tokens/sec for medium-length sessions. This ticket captures investigation steps, short-term mitigations, and a proposed long-term fix for kernel selection + prefetch heuristics.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send 1000 short-chat style requests (avg 30 tokens out) to hosted/redwood-v2-int8 in eu-west region over 5 minutes
2) Observe TTFT distribution: p50 increased from ~80ms to ~260ms; p95 spiked from ~220ms to ~620ms
3) Measure tokens/sec on worker side via /metrics token_output_rate: observed drop from baseline 12k -> 6.8k tokens/sec per GPU under similar concurrency
4) Repeat on Dedicated pool with same model variant and see comparable degradation under mixed-length traffic
observed_metrics: Tokens/sec: baseline 12k -> incident 6.8k (≈43% drop) for opt-2.7b-int8 workload profile
First-byte jitter: increase in inter-token latency at stream startup, correlated with kernel selection logs
KV-prefetch queue length: spikes coincident with kernel-selection churn
CPU-side scheduling: increased context switches in allocator threads during incident windows
investigation_notes: 03/09 22:15 UTC: Pager triggered by SE at AcmeCorp complaining of 3x TTFT for interactive flows (Hosted).
Collected logs: kernel_selector decisions show oscillation between kernel-v3 (vectorized) and kernel-v2 (fallback) for identical model shapes when concurrent short streams are present.
Hypothesis A: kernel selection heuristic is overfitting to bursty sequence-length signals causing head-of-line blocking and invalid warmstart reuse.
Hypothesis B: aggressive KV prefetching combined with per-tenant prefetch credits caused eviction storms when warmed weights were swapped, amplifying first-byte jitter.
Reproduced locally by replaying mixed-length traffic using k6 harness; enabling detailed kernel-selector debug correlates selection flips with transient queue depth > 200.
Noticed that Private deployments with older kernel packages (1.20.x) saw less severe impact, pointing to a regression in the selector heuristics introduced in 1.22.x.
No evidence of GPU memory pressure at incident time; GPU utilization remained within expected range but latency rose due to increased preempt/resume cycles.
mitigation: Hotpatch 1 (short-term): Pin kernel selector to stable-v2 heuristic across hosted pools for affected clusters (rolled to eu-west + us-west). Reduced TTFT p50 back toward baseline within 20 minutes.
Hotpatch 2 (safety): Deploy prefetch circuit-breaker that caps concurrent prefetch tasks per-tenant (soft cap 8 -> 4) to prevent eviction storms for long-tail contexts.
Rollback option: provided feature-flag to revert to runtime-1.21 kernel selection behavior; used for two Dedicated customer clusters as they required immediate SLA parity.
Customer communications: Notified impacted customers with timeline, temporary mitigations, and estimated ETA for full fix. Engineering on standby for additional rollouts.
proposed_fix: 1) Replace binary kernel-selection threshold with continuous scoring model that accounts for recent sequence-length distribution and warmstart hit rate.
2) Introduce a lightweight per-worker warmstart cache admission control that biases towards small-stream latency-sensitive items during high churn.
3) Adjust KV prefetch backoff: detect eviction oscillation patterns and apply exponential backoff on prefetch for tenants hitting eviction thresholds.
4) Add telemetry: expose kernel-selector flip-rate and warmstart-eviction-rate to Console dashboard for future alerts.
Estimated code change: kernel-selector service ~120 LOC + tests; prefetch backoff ~80 LOC + e2e. QA window: 3 days. Target runtime-1.22.4 release.
deployment_plan: Stage 1 (Canary): Deploy kernel-selector scoring model to 5% of hosted traffic in eu-west; monitor TTFT and tokens/sec for 2 hours.
Stage 2 (Regional ramp): If canary stable, roll to 50% eu-west, then to us-west. Keep Dedicated on pinned rollback until validation completes.
Stage 3 (Private): Provide patch package and instructions for on-prem/private customers; coordinate with Solutions Eng for scheduled maintenance windows.
Rollback strategy: If tokens/sec drops >10% or TTFT p95 increases >20% vs baseline during ramp, revert selector to stable-v2 heuristic immediately and disable prefetch changes.
Monitoring: create short-live Grafana dashboard for selector_flip_rate, prefetch_evictions, per-tenant token_rate, and an alert that fires when flip_rate > 5/min and eviction_rate > 2/min
postmortem_actions: Add unit+integration tests for kernel-selector under mixed-length traffic distributions
Create an automated chaos replay job that runs daily to detect selector oscillations with synthetic traffic
Ship Console UX alert to surface early warmstart-eviction signal to SRE and customers via email hooks
Doc: Update runbook for TTFT regressions with explicit steps to pin kernel heuristics and toggle prefetch circuit-breaker
